question: You are getting ready to transport an accident victim to the treatment room. What is the very first thing you must ensure?
explanation: Always remember: stabilize first, transport second! Moving a patient before checking their breathing or stopping severe bleeding can make things much worse. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h1)

question: When you and your team start moving a casualty, why is rushing strongly discouraged?
explanation: No need to run! Rushing makes it easy to trip, drop the patient, or twist an already injured spine. Slow, steady movements keep everyone safe. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h1)

question: When assessing an emergency patient using the famous ABCDE approach, what does the letter 'A' stand for?
explanation: A is always for Airway! Before anything else, we must check that air can freely flow into the patient's lungs without any blockage. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h2)

question: You suspect your patient has a neck injury from a fall. What device must you put on them before moving them?
explanation: Great job! A cervical collar gently keeps the neck in place so that any hidden spine injury doesn't get worse during movement. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h2)

question: Imagine you are rescuing someone from a rough, rocky bush path. Which equipment is best suited for this?
explanation: A rigid basket stretcher is built like a protective shell, keeping the patient safe and secure even over bumpy, uneven ground. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h3)

question: What is the special superpower of a scoop stretcher?

options.A: It doubles as an oxygen delivery system
options.B: It warms up cold trauma patients
options.C: It splits apart to slide under the patient

explanation: Scoop stretchers can separate into two halves. You simply slide them under the patient from the sides, meaning you don't have to awkwardly roll them over! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h3)

question: Your patient is awake and struggling to catch their breath. Which position will give them immediate relief?
explanation: Sitting them up a bit (Semi-Fowler's) lets gravity help their chest expand so they can breathe much easier. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h4)

question: An unconscious patient is breathing fine, but you need to transport them. What position should they be placed in?
explanation: The side-lying recovery position is a lifesaver here. It keeps their tongue from falling back and blocking the airway if they vomit or relax too much. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h4)

question: When lifting a heavy patient off a bed or trolley, which part of your body should do most of the heavy lifting?
explanation: Protect your back, nurse! Always bend your knees and use your strong thigh muscles to lift, keeping your back safe from strain. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h5)

question: Why do healthcare workers count down out loud (like '1, 2, 3, lift!') before moving a patient?

options.A: It keeps the ambulance driver on schedule
options.C: It ensures everyone lifts at the exact same moment
options.D: It helps calm down a frightened patient

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! A synchronized count prevents sudden jerks that could drop the patient or hurt someone on the team. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h5)

question: While moving a patient in an ambulance, what clinical check must you keep doing continuously?
explanation: Keep your eyes on the vital signs! Checking pulse, breathing, and blood pressure helps you catch any sudden changes right away. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of your core duties while transporting an emergency patient?
explanation: During transport, your job is to keep the patient stable and safe—figuring out the exact root diagnosis is usually left for the doctors at the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h6)

question: When handing over a patient to another nurse, what does the helpful memory tool ISBAR stand for?
explanation: ISBAR is your best friend for handovers. It structures your update so you never forget to share the most important facts with the incoming nurse. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h7)

question: Why is using a structured format like ISBAR so important when handing over a patient to a new ward?

options.A: It allows the receiving nurse to leave early
options.B: It proves who worked the longest shift
options.C: It replaces the need for a written medical chart
options.D: It prevents important patient details from being forgotten

explanation: A structured handover ensures clarity. It helps the receiving team instantly grasp what is going on without missing crucial care details. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h7)
